## Step 1: Understanding the concept of a write-ahead log
A write-ahead log, also known as a transaction log, is a data structure used by databases to ensure data consistency and recoverability. It is a record of all changes made to the database, including insertions, updates, and deletions. This log is "write-ahead" because any changes to the actual database are only committed after the corresponding entry has been written to the log.

## Step 2: Explaining the purpose of the log
The primary purpose of the write-ahead log is to enable a database to recover from a crash or failure by replaying the logged transactions. In the event of a failure, the database can read the log to determine which transactions were not completed before the failure occurred. By replaying these transactions, the database can restore its data to a consistent state.

## Step 3: Describing how the log works
When a transaction is committed, the database writes an entry to the log, including the transaction's ID, the type of operation (insert, update, or delete), and the data affected.
